transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. It's so nice to meet you too. Thank you for seeing me. 

Um, well, I guess what brings me in is... I just feel like I can’t quite settle in my own body anymore? It sounds a little silly to say out loud, and I'm sure it's probably not a huge deal, but I've just been feeling really restless lately. It happens especially when I’m supposed to just sit quietly and, you know, handle paperwork or sit down to go over shared household plans. I just can't seem to get comfortable doing those normal, everyday things. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Has this feeling of restlessness been something you've struggled with since you were a child, or is this a more recent change in your life?

Um, well... I guess if I really think about it, it's not exactly new? I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or a troublemaker, because I really did always try to be good! But... looking back, I think this was already a part of me back in elementary school. 

I was sort of, um, the girl with the messy desk, and I was always accidentally forgetting permission slips and things like that. And, well, I'd get notes from my teachers saying I talked out of turn or... or seemed unable to stay seated. I always felt so bad about it, but I just had a lot of energy, I guess? It wasn't on purpose. 

Is that the kind of thing you were asking? I hope that's helpful.
